store.js:30 Backup failure is swallowed while the load message tells the user the data was kept; the next save then destroys the original. backupRaw returns nothing, and the callers at store.js:47, 52 and 66 ignore the result. The messages at store.js:48, 53 and 67 state 'was kept under notes-backup' unconditionally. The comment claims the load message reports the failure, but those messages say the opposite. A backup is a second copy of a value that is already in storage, so it is the write most likely to hit the quota. Each backup also overwrites the previous one. Storage holds a corrupt or partly unreadable 3 MB 'notes' value in a ~5 MB quota. On load, setItem(BACKUP_KEY) throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed. The page shows 'The unreadable data was kept under notes-backup'. The user presses New note: saveNotes replaces the 'notes' value, and the original data exists nowhere, though they were told it was kept. A second corruption event later also overwrites the first backup with no warning.

app.js:223 The shared-notes fetch has no timeout, and the shared status is not cleared or reset when the query becomes empty. The server hangs. The user sees 'Searching shared notes…' forever, because only a newer query aborts the request. After the box is hidden and shown again for a new query, the old status text can briefly reappear.

store.js:30 Backup of corrupt data can fail silently while the user is told it was kept. backupRaw (store.js:29-31) swallows the setItem error and returns nothing. Its callers at store.js:47-48, 52-53 and 65-67 then return a problem string saying the data 'was kept under "notes-backup"'. The comment claims the load message reports the failure; it does not, because the message is written as if the backup succeeded. The raw value is already held under notes, so writing the backup needs about the same space again, and it fails once the stored data is more than about half of the quota. The first edit then overwrites STORAGE_KEY (store.js:75). Stored data is over 50% of the quota and fails JSON.parse, or holds one non-object entry. backupRaw throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed. The page says the data was kept under 'notes-backup'. The user creates a note, saveNotes replaces the key, and the original data is gone with no copy.

The 3 MB is unrecoverable and the user was told it was kept.

Nothing is backed up, because the backup only happens when notes are skipped.

store.js:50 loadNotes never checks data.version, so data written by a newer schema is read as version 1 and then overwritten in the old shape. A newer build saves {version: 2, notes: [...]} with extra fields or a different note shape. This build loads it, normalizeNote drops the unknown fields, and the next edit saves it back as version 1. The newer data is lost and no backup is made, because the backup only happens on parse failure or skipped notes.
Parse and reference errors: none. Every getElementById id in app.js exists in index.html. app.js relies on store.js loading first, and the script order in index.html is right.
Pending save: flushSave writes the id and values captured when the user typed. A note switch, delete or pagehide cannot write to the wrong note.
